advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure a regression guard for a371 executes under the bare `pytest` console script in the lean CI lane (no `[ui]`): either drop the `importorskip` from the subprocess test and assert the module skips-not-errors under `--collect-only`, or add a `[ui]`-installed CI lane so the subprocess guard actually runs.
evidence: .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:295 `uv sync --locked --extra dev` — only the `dev` extra is installed; `[ui]` (fastapi/httpx) is absent
Makefile:215 `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -q` — canonical bare-pytest invocation, run with the same lean install

The audit-page module runs `importorskip("fastapi")` at line 18 ABOVE the helper import, so the subprocess `--collect-only` cannot reach the formerly-broken import unless `[ui]` is installed; combined with the parent-process importorskip, the guard runs meaningfully ONLY where `[ui]` is present, which the CI/make-test lanes are not.
advisory.finding: The subprocess regression guard `test_audit_page_modules_collect_under_bare_pytest` gates itself on `pytest.importorskip('fastapi')`/`('httpx')`, so it SKIPS in the lean CI suite and `make test` lane (which install only the `dev` extra, not `[ui]`) — the exact environment where bug a371 was invisible. The one test that directly reproduces the reported `ModuleNotFoundError` under the bare `pytest` console script therefore provides no regression coverage in the lane that would have caught the original break.
